scope: The AP-side transport that carries CI primitives from atcmdsrv to the CP, recovered statically from firmware 3.0.2 Build 241129 Rel.3n. Companion to analysis/ci-primitives.json, which owns the service-group and primitive-id namespace. No message was ever sent.

chain: per-command builder, e.g. atcmdsrv 0x40cac for CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_REQ
0x7e2c4  marshaller: sizes, allocates, fills the envelope, logs, hands off
0x7f178 -> 0x139d0 (PLT)  socket write on the msocket fd

entry_signature.args: r0 = CI client object, r1 = numeric primId, r2 = reqHandle, r3 = pointer to the primitive payload (may be NULL for zero-length primitives)
entry_signature.guard: `cmp.w r4, #0x11111111` at 0x7cd34 rejects a poisoned/uninitialised client object and returns 8.

wire_format.total_length: 0x1c + payloadLen; the whole buffer is written to the socket

fields.name: envelope_type
fields.value: message type discriminator; 4 = CI primitive, 3 = handler registration

fields.name: primitive_id
fields.evidence: 0x7e316 `strh r6,[r0,#0x10]` - note the id is 16-bit on the wire, which is why the 0xF000 error range fits

fields.name: pad
fields.evidence: not written; implied by the 16-byte inner header

fields.name: reserved
fields.confidence: NEGATIVE EVIDENCE on the mapped paths - never written by the sender and never read by the AP RX dispatcher. Not audited on the CP side. Do not name it.

wire_format.note: The inner header is exactly 16 bytes (0x0c..0x1c), matching `inner_length = 0x10 + payloadLen`. The outer 12 bytes are the msocket envelope.

payload_sizing.rule: If primId - 0xF000 <= 7, the size comes from the global CI_ERR u16 table at 0x0bdc3a. Otherwise a tbb switch on svgId-1 selects the group's own u16 size table, bounds-checks primId, and reads size = table[primId].
payload_sizing.size_table_root: 0x0e1084; per-group pointers at +0x04 CC, +0x08 SS, +0x0c MM, +0x10 PB, +0x14 SIM, +0x18 MSG, +0x1c PS, +0x24 DEV
special_cases: DAT (svgId 8) has no size table; sizes are computed at run time by 0x7ef30 from the payload.
DEV primId 0x47 (CI_DEV_PRIM_ENABLE_HSDPA_REQ) is hardcoded to 9 at 0x7f05e.
PS primId 0x42 is hardcoded to 0x5c at 0x7f062.
payload_sizing.confidence: CONFIRMED - the table value for DEV/51 is 32, matching the `movs r2,#0x20` allocation in the SET_BAND_MODE builder.

device_nodes.note: These three nodes are NOT interchangeable. Only msocket is on the CI request path.

/dev/msocket.role: CONFIRMED: the CI message transport. The fd used by 0x7d0aa is a global set up by the opener at 0x7f074, whose only device string is /dev/msocket (referenced from the literal pool at 0x7f158).
/dev/msocket.carries: metadata and payload together, in one contiguous write

/dev/acipc.role: Referenced once, from 0x5ee4c, in a component unrelated to the CI send path.
/dev/acipc.assessment: SUPPORTED INFERENCE: ACIPC is the underlying AP/CP doorbell/signalling substrate that msocket is layered on, not a separate message channel used by atcmdsrv. The CP side names ACIPCDHISR/ACIPCRDHISR/acipcTx.

/dev/cpmem.role: Referenced from 0x72928 and 0x7f924, outside the CI send path.
/dev/cpmem.assessment: UNKNOWN whether CI payloads ever transit shared memory. On this path they do not: the payload is copied inline into the msocket write.

dispatcher.role: The AP-side CI confirmation/indication demultiplexer. Every CNF, IND and CI_ERR returning from the CP passes through here.

rx_message_struct.note: The struct the dispatcher receives, after the msocket frame parser has unpacked the wire envelope. Field roles are fixed by how the dispatcher passes them on.

fields.name: request handle
fields.evidence: 0x7ee56 `ldr r3,[r4,#8]`, passed as arg3 and decoded as a handle by every group handler

dispatch_rule.table: atcmdsrv .bss 0x000eeb94, one function pointer per service group id
dispatch_rule.lookup: 0x7ee4e `ldr.w r5,[r0, r1, lsl #2]` with r1 = svgId
dispatch_rule.null_handling: A NULL slot falls through to 0x7ee76, which logs and drops the message. There is no fallback handler.
dispatch_rule.logging: 0x7ee46 calls the same decoder (0x7ddec) used on the send path, so RX and TX share one symbolic view of (svgId, primId).

handler_registration.registrar: atcmdsrv 0x5a344 builds one 36-byte record per service group; 0x7ccd4 -> 0x7d9cc message type 3 installs it.
handler_registration.handler_source: The RX handler pointer comes from the static table at 0x0977ac indexed by service group id, so 0x000eeb94[svgId] is fully predictable.
handler_registration.supersedes: The earlier statement that the handler pointers 'cannot be resolved from static data alone' is wrong and is retracted. The registration is data-driven, but the data is a static table.

envelope_types.3: register a service-group handler set (installed locally AND forwarded to the CP)
envelope_types.5: register the global catch-all handler pair
envelope_types.6: clear the global catch-all handler pair
envelope_types.note: The outer envelope's second word is a message-type discriminator on a shared msocket control channel, not a constant.

reserved_header_bytes.offset: 0x18 of the wire buffer (the last 4 bytes of the 16-byte inner header)
reserved_header_bytes.finding: Never written on the send path and never read by the RX dispatcher, which consumes only the payload pointer, svgId, primId and reqHandle. The four bytes are left at whatever the allocator returned.
reserved_header_bytes.caution: This is 'unused on the mapped paths', not 'unused by the protocol'. The CP side was not audited for a reader. Do not name the field.

dev_request_dispatch_table.form: 76 entries of {u32 primId, u32 handler|1}, 8-byte stride, extent 0x06f394fc .. 0x06f3977c
dev_request_dispatch_table.verification: Every id resolves to a CI_DEV_PRIM_*_REQ name; primId 0x33 pairs with 0x068afdf1, independently proven to be the SET_BAND_MODE handler by its 0x34 CNF and 32-byte request validation.

internal_signal_table.form: {u32 handler, u32 signalId} pairs with ids around 0x00090c1b-0x00090c21
internal_signal_table.assessment: A distinct CP-internal signal namespace, not CI primitive ids. CI_DEV_PRIM_GET_BAND_MODE_CNF is built by 0x068b0156, which appears in this table rather than the CI table - consistent with the CNF being emitted asynchronously once lower layers respond.

safety: Recovery only. No CI primitive, AT command, or socket write was executed, and no device was contacted.

req_handle.status: CONFIRMED field map; two fields have confirmed use, two are partially understood
req_handle.construction: Built in each AT command handler's prologue (AT*BAND at 0x38152, +COPS at 0x18e4c, +CPLMNS at 0x18f5c - all identical code).

fields.name: transaction counter
fields.detail: 12-bit counter in a static halfword, incremented per request. It wraps 0xfff -> 0x0b, not to 0, so the low 12 bits are never 0..0x0a after the first wrap.

fields.name: AT session / channel index
fields.detail: 8 bits, from the AT session object shifted left 12 and masked with 0xff000. Consumers extract it with `ubfx rX, handle, #12, #8` and use it as an array index - e.g. atcmdsrv 0x2c8d2 computes `base + 0x34 * index` into a per-session context array, and the MM handler passes it to 0x2a8ac at 0x1d660.

fields.name: caller request tag
fields.detail: 10-bit tag chosen by the request builder, which first clears bits 20-29 and 31. Most builders set it to the primitive id (0x33/0x35/0x37 for band mode, 0x14 for the operator-count scan, 0xca for PS primitive 202), but not all: atcmdsrv 0x2c8e4 sets 0x103 while sending PS primitive 9. Confirmation handlers read it back with `ubfx r3, handle, #20, #10` and compare - e.g. the MM handler tests `== 0xca` at 0x1dbcc - to tell apart different internal callers of the same primitive.
fields.confidence: CONFIRMED as a caller-defined tag; NEGATIVE EVIDENCE against it being strictly the primitive id

fields.name: session class
fields.detail: 2 bits, from the return value of 0x5ce80(sessionObject) shifted left 30. The MM handler tests bit 30 at 0x1d676 and selects between two different context-table bases accordingly. Bit 31 is cleared by every builder's `bic #0xbf000000`.
fields.confidence: SUPPORTED INFERENCE for the meaning; CONFIRMED for the construction and the two-way branch

req_handle.not_a_bit_puzzle: The handle is a composite routing key, not an opaque id: bits 12-19 select the originating AT session, bits 20-29 select which internal caller within that session, and bits 0-11 disambiguate concurrent requests. That is enough to route a CNF back to its caller without any per-request allocation table.
req_handle.unknown: Whether the CP inspects any part of the handle, or only echoes it.
